body: In October 2024, the City of South Bend, acting at the direction of its mayor, filed a complaint to condemn real property owned by Argos 316, LLC in a redevelopment project area established by the South Bend Redevelopment Commission. Portage Township of St. Joseph County had already contracted to buy the property and completed the purchase shortly after the City filed. The Township and 350 Columbia Street, LLC, which held easements on the property, intervened and objected that the action was not authorized by the South Bend Common Council, as Indiana Code section 36-7-14-20(a) contemplates. The Marshall Circuit Court, Judge Janette E. Surrisi presiding, overruled the objection, concluding that Council authorization is one way, not the only way, for the City to condemn property in a redevelopment project area.

The Court of Appeals reversed in an opinion by Judge Nancy H. Vaidik, joined by Judge May. The City argued that the statute only sets a procedure for when the legislative body chooses to act and leaves other officials' broad condemnation power under Indiana Code section 36-1-4-5(a) intact; the objectors argued it confines the power to the legislative body. Finding both readings reasonable on the text alone, the court looked to the surrounding chapter, which sets out how a redevelopment commission is created, how a project area is designated with plan commission and legislative body approval, and how the commission must first try to negotiate purchases. Read as a whole, the redevelopment scheme "makes clear that the power lies with the unit's legislative body," the court wrote.

Because the Common Council never authorized the action, the court held the trial court erred in overruling the objection, and it did not reach the objectors' other arguments. Chief Judge Tavitas concurred in the result, noting that neither party had argued the statute was ambiguous.

timeline.label: South Bend files a condemnation complaint against the Argos 316 property; Portage Township completes its purchase of the property shortly afterward
Court of Appeals reverses, holding only the Common Council could authorize the condemnation
